## Research

Kayode's research asks how far a measurement can be trusted, and what that trust is worth to a decision. He studies uncertainty quantification for AI and for low-cost sensing, with a focus on places where data is scarce.

He is a PhD researcher in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at Imperial College London (2026 to present), supervised by Professor Wouter Buytaert. He works in the Schmidt Sciences Virtual Institute for Earth's Water (VIEW) on the project "Unlocking Local Knowledge Production for Global Water Reanalysis", co-led by Imperial and the International Water Management Institute (IWMI), with field sites in Ghana, Ethiopia, Ecuador, India, Laos and Peru. The work combines community-measured rainfall, river levels, flow and groundwater with historical records and models.

## Projects

- ng-flood (2026): turns Google's riverine and flash-flood forecasts into location-level warnings for Nigeria, grouped by NIPOST postcode area. Every verdict records the gauge and forecast used, and site locations stay on the user's machine.
- Community-sensed flood warning (2026): flood warnings for dense informal settlements such as Ajegunle, Lagos, where satellite radar cannot see standing water. Uses TESSERA geospatial foundation-model embeddings as a spatial prior and residents' reports in English, Nigerian Pidgin or Yoruba with a sequential probability ratio test. Presented at London Geo Meetup, Birkbeck (August 2026); tutorial prepared for the NeurIPS 2026 Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning workshop.
- WazoCore (2026): adds 15,000 Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo tokens to N-ATLaS, Nigeria's open language model, giving 1.55 to 1.64 times faster generation in llama.cpp.
- gagelink and quantity-guard (2026): an MCP server giving AI agents river level, streamflow, flood forecasts and basins from USGS, NOAA, Hub'Eau, the UK Environment Agency and SWOT, with units, vertical datum and quality attached. In 4,288 runs across eleven models, unguarded agents passed ft3/s as m3/s, a 35.3 times error.
- Removing Data Leakage Does Not Fix Benchmarks (2026): manuscript and code showing that when shortcut pathways are redundant, removing one identified leak leaves the metric unchanged. Introduces provclose, a diagnostic package tested across twelve river basins.
- Riverlabs firmware (2026): contributions to Imperial's open-source firmware for low-cost river-level loggers.
- Katcha Ward flood study (2026): a six-year Sentinel-1 flood record for 8,891 ha of rice farmland on the River Niger floodplain, identifying 4,109 ha at highest hazard and guiding distribution of flood-tolerant FARO 67 rice seed.
